haiku.problem: The pronoun "his" comes before Abraham is named, which breaks the rule against using he/she/they/his before saying who it is. Name him first, e.g. "Abraham's last plea..."

The set omits card 1-8, where Abraham steps forward and asks whether the LORD will sweep away the righteous with the wicked. That is the central question of the passage, and all four questions cover only the LORD's replies and numbers.
